timecoded_text_to_speech.text: This is the Meteor Report for the Automated Media Camera operated by the Craven Manor
House Astronomical Society, Dabbed, the month of September 2020.
This month we detected a total of 269 meteors, while over half were sporadics, with meteors
from known showers only making a minor contribution to the total.
The largest identified shower came from the September Perseids, but contributed only 22
meteors.
A special report on the August Perseid meter shower is available from the IN video link.
The meteors in this video are shown in chronological order.
The brightest detected was of magnitude minus 2.6 and a total of 26 different showers
were identified.
There is a particularly nice meteor, which leaves a brief trail full for September at 3.07
a.m.
Our data has been collated by the Society's Meteor team and passed on to the nematode
meteor group with further analysis, triangulates the same meteors observed by different observatories
to produce orbital information for the meteor, further enhancing our knowledge of the
space around Earth's orbit.
Our setup is relatively simple.
A single WattEC video camera connected to a PC running UFO analyzer detects meteor candidates.
These are copied to a network attached storage device which has a web interface.
The Society members access this cloud drive and delete any false positive detections.
This way the members can contribute whilst at home and share the burden of sifting through
the potential meteors.
At the end of the month, one member runs analysis of the meteors and these data are passed
on to the nematode group.
The meteors are located at headquarters at Sutton at home.
A hardware, software and internet connection are all funded by the Society and all members
of the Society are encouraged to take part.
The more people interested in contributing, the more cameras we can have.
So if you are a member and want to take part, please contact Jenny Smakling.
The Craved Manor House Astronomical Society Dartford meet every Thursday currently via
Zoom due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Most evenings consist of a professional lecture by academics, space scientists or well-known
and talented amateurs followed by member observations and other society business.
If you'd like to take part, please contact our secretary at CravedManorAstro.com.
I'd love to know which of the meteors you think are the best in September.
Please leave a comment below with the timestamp of your favourite.
If you've enjoyed this video, please leave a thumbs up.
If you have a question, please comment.
And if you'd like to see more of these videos, please subscribe.
Thanks for watching.
